newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Greencore says annual profit to fall this yr.
newsitem.headline: Greencore says annual profit to fall this yr.

text.p: Irish agribusiness firm Greencore Group Plc said on Wednesday its pre-exceptional profits for the year would be "somewhat lower" than last year.

Chairman Bernie Cahill said second-half profits would be damaged by a recent eight-week strike which affected its sugar operations and a boycott of its fertiliser business sparked by a dispute with sugar beet growers over prices.

"These events, while now behind us, will nevertheless adversely affect our second-half trading," he said in a statement. "Profit for the year before exceptional items is likely to be somwhat lower than last year."

Greencore announced first-half pre-tax profits of 22 million punts, down 15 percent on the same period a year ago. Profits were hit by an exceptional charge of 5.8 million punts, resulting from a European Commission fine of seven million punts offset by a 1.2 million profit from the sale of two non-core businesses.
Cahill said that despite the adverse events that would impact on annual profits, the company's longer term outlook was good.
"The underlying strength of our business...continues to improve," he said. "Industrial demand in our home market for ingredients such as sugar, flour and malt continues to be strong."
Cahill said the trading environment in the agribusiness sector should improve as current difficulties in the beef and dairy industries recede.

"The adverse trading conditions encountered by our grain businesses in the current year are not expected to recur at the 1997 harvest," he said. "Our food businesses continue to trade well and the prospects for our associates are good."
Greencore said that although first-half profits had been hit by revaluations of the green Irish pound sparked by the strength of the Irish currency, currency pressures had abated in recent weeks.
Chief executive David Dilger said the half-year results had been good despite difficult conditions.
"The group has again recorded good operating profit and headline earnings per share growth despite the adverse impact of currency movements on our selling prices," he said.

"During the early part of our second half we have had to deal with several abnormal issues. These issues are now behind us and we look forward to demonstrating again the quality of our businesses and our profit streams."
